''rigens'']] }} '''''Orobanche rapum-genistae''''', the '''greater broomrape''',{{cite web |url=http://sppaccounts.bsbi.org/content/orobanche-rapum-genistae-0.html |title=''Orobanche rapum-genistae'' |author=Lockton, A.J. |work=BSBI Species account |publisher=Botanical Society of the British Isles |access-date=12 April 2020}} is a plant species in the genus ''[[Orobanche]]''. It is a [[Parasitism#Plants|parasitic plant]], native to Europe, growing on the roots of plants in the [[Fabaceae|bean]] family, usually [[Cytisus scoparius|common broom]] or [[Ulex europaeus|European gorse]]. ==Description== The broomrapes are perennial, [[Parasitism|parasitic]] plants which contain no [[chlorophyll]] and are totally dependent on other plants to provide their nutrients. The greater broomrape can grow to a height of {{convert|3|ft|m|0|abbr=on}} with a honey-brown downy stem, persisting as a dark brown dead spike after flowering. The leaves are represented by small pointed scales, concentrated near the base of the stem, and there is a single bract, which is longer than the flower, below each flower. These have a [[Petal|corolla]] with two lips, four stamens and a curved-down style. The upper lip is hooded and the lower lip has three lobes, the central one being the largest. The fruits are egg-shaped and enclosed in the dead flowerhead, and the seeds are minute.{{cite book |last1=McClintock |first1=David |last2=Fitter |first2=R.S.R. |year=1961 |title=The Pocket Guide to Wild Flowers |publisher=Collins |publication-place=London |page=148 }} ==Distribution and habitat== The greater broomrape is a parasitic plant, growing on the roots of leguminous shrubs, and is to be found only where its [[Host (biology)|host]] plants are found; these are usually [[Ulex europaeus|European gorse]] or [[Cytisus scoparius|common broom]], but occasionally it grows on [[Genista tinctoria|dyer's greenweed]]. It has a suboceanic, southern-temperate distribution,{{cite web |url=https://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/plant/orobanche-rapum-genistae |title=''Orobanche rapum-genistae1'' |work=Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora |access-date=16 March 2020}} in Western Europe and North Africa; in France, the Netherlands and Belgium it is widespread, but in Germany it occurs mainly in the west, and in Switzerland in montane and sub-alpine settings. It occurs all over Italy, and is present in Corsica and Algeria.{{cite journal |author=Foley, M.J.Y. |year=2000 |title= A morphological comparison between some British ''Orobanche'' species (Orobanchaceae) and their closely-related, non-British counterparts from continental Europe: ''Orobanche rapum-genistae'' Thuill. s.l. |journal=Watsonia |volume=23 |pages=413–419 |url=http://archive.bsbi.org.uk/Wats23p413.pdf }} In Britain it is present in scattered locations, mostly in Wales, Southwest England and near the coast in South England. It was in decline in the 18th and early 19th centuries, but more recently has staged a revival. It grows in the [[Great Casterton Road Banks]], an [[SSSI]] in Lincolnshire.{{cite web|url=https://necmsi.esdm.co.uk/PDFsForWeb/Citation/1001890.pdf |title=Great Casterton Road Banks citation|series= Sites of Special Scientific Interest|publisher=Natural England|access-date= 16 March 2020}} ==Chemistry== ''Orobanche rapum-genistae'' contains [[verbascoside]] and [[orobanchoside]].{{cite journal |author=Andary, C. |author2=Wyldea, R. |author3=Laffitea, C. |author4=Privat, G. |author5=Winternitza, F. |year=1982 |title=Structures of verbascoside and orobanchoside, caffeic acid sugar esters from ''Orobanche rapum-genistae'' |journal=Phytochemistry |volume=21 |issue=5 |pages=1123–1127 |doi=10.1016/S0031-9422(00)82429-2}} File:Orobanche rapum-genistae1.jpg|Flowers File:Orobanche rapum-genistae flor.jpg|Detail flower File:Orobanche rapum-genistae fruto.jpg|Detail fruit File:Orobanche rapum-genistae02.jpg File:Ginster-SommerwurzDetail.jpg ==References== {{Commons}} {{Wikispecies}} {{Reflist}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q161785}} [[Category:Orobanche|rapum-genistae]] [[Category:Plants described in 1799]]
